text: Bob Dylan has 40 studio albums and about 600 songs.
A website about him is mostly a data problem:
write the pages by hand, and they are wrong in a month.
The obvious build is a template site:
5 pages, the biography as one long wall of text,
and no link from a song to its album or its year.
The plan has 6 parts: content files,
a data build that checks and links them,
a generator that makes the pages,
a search index, hosting, and a design system.
Step 1, the content model.
One file per album, song and event.
A song file names its album,
and a validator fails the build if that album does not exist.
Not a CMS: this site has 2 editors.
First choice: how much content before launch?
10 albums: we launch in 2 weeks and learn what readers open.
All 40: a month of data entry before anyone sees the site.
I recommend 10.
Which do you want?
With 10 albums, steps 2 to 6 start next week.
With all 40, every later step waits about a month.
Next, part 2: the data build and the generator.
Part 2 of 3.
10 albums is banked, and everything from here reads from those files.
Step 2, the data build.
It reads every file, follows every reference,
and writes one index: site.json.
An album knows its songs; an era knows its albums and events.
A song that names a missing album fails the build here,
not on a visitor's screen.
Quick check.
A song names an album that does not exist.
Empty link, build fails, or song skipped?
Step 3, the generator.
It turns site.json into pages: one per era,
one per album, one per song,
and a timeline.
Every page is plain HTML, so a phone needs no JavaScript to read it.
We use Astro; Next.js would ship JavaScript the site does not need.
Second choice: is the timeline in the first release?
As a list by year, it is one template,
and the events already exist.
Without it, the era pages lose their links to the years around an album.
I recommend the list.
Which do you want?
With the timeline, every era page links to its years.
Without it, the generator has 3 page kinds,
and the eras stand alone.
Next, part 3: design, search, hosting,
and the plan resolved.
Part 3 of 3.
The timeline is in, and now the pages need a look.
Step 4, the design system.
2 kinds of page: a biography,
read like a book in one narrow column;
and an album page, a reference,
full width with a table of tracks.
One serif, one sans, images in 2 sizes.
Third choice: the look of the reading pages.
Here they are side by side.
Book-like: a serif, wide margins, few images;
cheap to do well.
Magazine: big photographs and bold headings;
striking, but the photographs are copyrighted,
and we may not be allowed to use them.
I recommend book-like.
Which do you want?
Book-like: one serif face, wide margins,
and no photographs to clear.
Magazine: big photographs on every page,
and a rights check before launch.
Step 5, search.
The build writes a small index,
about 60 kilobytes, and the browser loads it the first time you click the
search box.
No search server.
Step 6, hosting.
Push to main and the site builds and deploys;
a pull request gets a preview link.
Adding an album is one file.
That is the plan, with your 3 choices.
Draw on any step to ask for a change,
or approve it.
